127541488.author: NormanRus
127541488.text: It's often said that first impressions are important, and I think that's applicable for many things, creating included. The first part of a level sets the bar for the rest of it, so it's critical that this portion is polished, detailed, and impressive. OoOhh did a great job with this concept, and the first part of the level set several expectations; some of these were fulfilled, while others could be great ideas for improvements.The color and design choices feel fantastic in a large portion of this level! I want to specifically dissect the 40-56% part as I speak on this, because there was a wonderful color scheme set here, as well as sensible deigns and air decoration which made the part feel very complete. The pallete chosen resembled a sunset in the background, which was emulated using a Gradient trigger blended with some glow at the top of the player's visibility; several clouds were also included, moving at different speeds, which provided depth for the visuals. The designs read as nature-inspired, being dark, rocky blocks topped with lighter grass and two-toned spikes. There were some trees and windmills included in the middle ground, which offered extra details that filled space well. There were some pulses that made the song feel represented, but they weren't overbearing, which was nice. The part was followed up with a transition that read as complete and polished. I said that some expectations I gathered from the first part weren't carried out in the rest of the level, and the main one that missed the mark was the coherence of the level. The quality and theming felt all over the place, and the most serious dip in quality lied in the second part. This portion lacked the color contrast and design theory that the other portions mastered. Looking at a broader scope, some parts focus more on designs and others hone in on effects, which makes for a bit of a choppy focal point as the player experiences the level. If I were to be the creator of this, I would start by revising the second part, and then make the final part (everything after 60%) less flash-oriented I appreciate a lot of OoOhh's parts and the attention to detail they featured. However, I really wish that the two halves of the project didn't feel like two separate levels, and I'd love to see some cleaning up of the second part. I do think that the level has potential, and each of these parts offers something unique that suggests clear creative talent.
